## Questions and action decisions

- No questions were asked. The audience, format, product facts, CTA and scope were sufficient to produce a complete draft.
- Selected `sdcorejs-content` for one small social-video draft, with TikTok, short-video and tech references. No engineering spec, plan, test suite or Git workflow was introduced.
- Treated the supplied capabilities as user-supplied facts, not independently verified facts.
- Removed the unsupported speed claim, customer-count claim and testimonial from the usable script. The separate note states what evidence would be needed to use them.
- Used a fictional API example and an explicitly illustrative teammate question. The comment is demo content, not a customer quote or endorsement.
- Kept the demo to storage and comments. Included the stated limits in the spoken script and avoided execution or generated-code imagery.
- Used a low-pressure invitation, “Curious? Explore QueryLane.” No invented URL, pricing, free trial or sign-up claim.
- Manually reviewed factual support, audience fit, practical progression, readable captions and the proportional CTA before saving. Exact interface details remain unspecified because no UI source was supplied.
- Saved the script only because the worker explicitly requires `outputs/response.md`. No voice-profile persistence or target repository writes.

## Execution boundaries and limitations

Executed: scoped local reference reads, drafting, local output writing, editorial review and the recorded text verification.

Proposed only: every shot, fictional example, demonstration comment, caption and timing beat. No media was created or captured. No account was accessed; no network requests, messages, posting, scheduling, Git operations or additional agents were used.

The 20-second duration is an editorial production estimate. No read-aloud recording, rendered timing test, actual-product execution, customer validation or benchmark was performed. The draft explicitly labels these limits where material.
